newsitem.title: USA: Broward Cty, Fla., seeks $800 mln school bond vote.
newsitem.headline: Broward Cty, Fla., seeks $800 mln school bond vote.

text.p: Florida's Broward County School Board voted to hold a November referendum on up to $800 million of general obligation bonds for schools.

The school board approved the referendum Tuesday after months of debate. Board Chairman Abe Fischler said the panel would release a detailed plan by May setting the size of the issue and listing projects it would fund.

The board also voted to change the way board members are elected. Currently, all seven are elected at large. If approved by voters, the change would expand the board to nine members, electing six from single-member districts and three at large.
The agreement on the bond referendum came after several minority and civic groups said they would support the bond issue if the board also put the districting question on the ballot.

The school board also tentatively agreed to let the city of Pembroke Pines build two new schools and lease them back to the countywide school district. The city had complained that the school board was not moving quickly enough to ease severe crowding at schools in the rapidly growing community.
The plan also calls for the city to give $3 million of development fee revenue to the school board to provide technology for east Broward schools outside Pembroke Pines.

The board must vote again on final approval once legal details are worked out. Bond counsel Michael Krul cautioned that the use of development fees outside the city limit may be illegal because the fees were collected in a special assessment district and must be spent there.
